title: metered pi dispatch depends on pi's stored Workers AI key being valid upstream
body:
The generated gateway override stamps cf-aig-authorization with the account token, but the gateway forwards pi's own Authorization (its stored cloudflare-workers-ai credential) to Workers AI. Live, a bogus Authorization plus a valid cf-aig-authorization logs a failed row with upstream 10000 Authentication error. On a host whose pi stores the cfu_ wallet key (as this one did during dm2), enabling metering turns every Workers AI dispatch into a 401, not just an unmetered one. A headers.Authorization entry in the override does displace pi's stored key (verified locally against a fake server), so the fix is small, but choosing the credential that pays is an operator decision. The dm2 comments in pimeter.go/pimeter_test.go that say the stored key cannot be displaced and is 'used or ignored by the gateway' are wrong on both counts and should be corrected with it.
evidence: internal/exec/subprocess/pimeter.go: gatewayCredentialCommand doc comment; live probe t648-probe-e (gateway row success=false, response code 10000)
